I've been working this land for 45 years. I know what this soil wants, I know the rains, and I know what prices look like at the market in autumn. Let me think through what I'll do this year.

**Wheat and Maize**

The wheat-maize rotation is the backbone of my household income. I'll put 5 mu into this system. Come October, I'll plant wheat — I switched to improved varieties years ago, everyone here uses them now, the yield difference is too big to ignore. I'll plough after the maize harvest to break up the compaction, then rotary till before seeding. I do three irrigations: the winter watering before freeze, the jointing water in spring, and one more at grain fill. Fertilizer — I spread urea and compound fertilizer the way my neighbors do, about 18 kg of nitrogen equivalent per mu, some phosphorus and potassium at planting. After wheat harvest in June I'll plant maize directly into the stubble, no deep ploughing. Hybrid seed, same as last year. Two or three watering depending on whether it rains. Maize I don't spray much — maybe once or twice if there's pest pressure.

**Cotton**

I've grown cotton my whole life. I'll keep 2.7 mu of it. It's hard work now at my age, but I know it well and the price was acceptable last year. I'll spring-plough it deep, plant hybrid Bt cotton in late April. Cotton needs more water and more fertilizer than people think — especially potassium, I've learned that over the years. I'll irrigate 4 times through the season, spray 4-5 times for pests and disease, though the Bt variety handles bollworm mostly on its own now.
